title: stochastic-batch-gating-and-microburst-smoothing-lab-notes
content:
Summary:

Quick notes from the gated-batching experiment run on 2024-05-20 -> 2024-05-28. We explored a lightweight stochastic gating layer added to the continuous batcher to smooth microbursts and reduce P99 tail spikes while preserving average throughput. Idea: instead of fixed timeouts or strict size thresholds, introduce a probabilistic gate that delays low-urgency requests by a small, randomly sampled window conditioned on instantaneous queue features.

Why we tried this:
- Persistent P99 spikes during microbursts (10-30ms arrival floods) that existing timeouts either over-flush (wasting compute) or under-aggregate (high tail).
- Deterministic heuristics (hard threshold, fixed timeout) create pathological synchronization between tenants. Stochastic gating may decorrelate arrivals and allow natural smoothing without huge config complexity.

Experiment design (high-level):
- Baseline: continuous-batcher (stable) with 8ms flush timeout and size cap 32.
- Variant A (gate-prob): for each incoming request r, compute gate_prob = sigmoid(alpha * (queue_depth - q0) + beta * urgency_score). With probability gate_prob we hold r for an extra sampled hold_time ~ Exp(lambda) capped at hold_max.
- Variant B (burst-detect + smoothing): detect microburst when arrivals in 10ms window > burst_thresh; during burst, increase hold_time by factor gamma and bias gate_prob downward for urgent classes.
- Variant C (fair-gate): same as A but include per-tenant slowdown counter to avoid starving small tenants; gate probability reduced for tenants with high slowdown.

Workloads and replay:
- Production replay trace (billing/embedding-heavy) trimmed to 5-minute segments showing 3 microbursts (observed in prod logs).
- Synthetic microburst generator: base Poisson with lambda=200 req/s plus 30ms burst spikes to 2500 req/s. Request length distribution: 8-512 tokens. Mix includes chat (interactive) and batch-embed flows.

Key metrics captured (instrumentation):
- Latency: P50/P90/P95/P99 (total), Scheduling latency, kernel latency (inference only).
- Throughput: tokens/sec, requests/sec, GPU occupancy.
- Fairness: max slowdown (tenant_p99_latency / tenant_baseline), starvation_count (requests delayed > 500ms).
- Cost proxies: avg batch size, wasted slots (empty capacity due to premature flush).

Important config knobs tried:
- alpha in [-0.02, 0.02] (controls responsiveness to queue_depth)
- beta in [-1.0, 1.0] (urgency weight)
- lambda for Exp in [50, 400] (ms^-1 scale -> mean hold_time between 2.5ms and 20ms)
- hold_max = {10, 30, 60} ms
- burst_thresh = {15, 30, 50} arrivals per 10ms window
- gamma = {1.5, 3.0}

Results (aggregated highlights):
- Baseline: P99 = 214ms, P95 = 96ms, avg batch size = 7.1, GPU occ ~72%.
- Variant A (alpha=0.01, beta=-0.3, lambda=120ms^-1, hold_max=30ms): P99 = 156ms (~27% reduction), P95 = 88ms (~8% reduction), avg batch size = 8.9 (+25%), GPU occ ~76%. Starvation_count ~= 2/5m (acceptable).
- Variant B (burst detect burst_thresh=30, gamma=3.0): P99 = 132ms (~38% reduction vs baseline), but P95 slightly worse for interactive class (tradeoff). GPU occ increased to 80%.
- Variant C (fair-gate with tenant slowdown correction): P99 = 141ms, P95 = 92ms. Max slowdown reduced from 2.1x (Variant B) to 1.25x. Small tenants no longer hit >300ms backlog. Throughput similar to B.

Observations and hypotheses:
- Stochastic gating reduces synchronization between inflight arrivals; batch sizes grow modestly but consistent, which lowers kernel amortized overhead and reduces tail.
- Microburst-specific smoothing (Variant B) is very effective at the precise moments that make P99 blow up. However, it unfairly penalizes the shortest, latency-sensitive requests unless we correct for tenant/urgency.
- Fairness correction (Variant C) recovers small-tenant latency while keeping most tail improvements. The slowdown counter design (exponential decay, half-life ~30s) seems stable across runs.
- We saw a small number of pathological rare cases where gating held high-urgency requests because urgency scoring was stale in the cache. Need to ensure the urgency_score is always recomputed on requeue.

Microtrace example (one burst):
- 00:01:12.345 -> 00:01:12.375: 18 arrivals in 30ms. Baseline: immediate flushes create 18 tiny batches -> GPU idle/warm overhead -> P99 spike 420ms across a few tenants.
- Variant B: gate kicks in, coalesces to 5 batches of size ~4-5, GPU kernels amortized, P99 reduced to 98ms. But one tenant with urgency tag 'interactive' saw median increase from 14ms to 32ms; fixed in Variant C.

Instrumentation notes:
- Added small counter tags on request structs: original-arrival-ts, gate-decisions, hold-sampled-ms, requeue-count. These made debugging much easier. Keep these for further experiments.
- Need lightweight aggregation at worker-level to avoid blowing Prom card counts (use rollup every 10s).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Tunable default: alpha=0.01 and hold_max=30ms looked robust across traces, but we need larger matrix (more workloads) before promoting.
- How do these gates interact with kv-cache heavy workloads where sequence length dominates kernel time? If kernel time >> hold_time, batching decisions may be less impactful. We should test with long-context workloads (2k tokens).
- Evaluate safety with private deployments (VPC latency variance) and Dedicated (higher throughput instances).
- Explore combining gating with adaptive prefill: if gate pushes more concurrency, kernel prefill heuristics should adapt to avoid memory spikes.

Action items (short):
- [Aisha] run 10x more synthetic scenarios with varied long-tail sequence lengths and multiple tenant mixes (due 2024-06-09).
- [Ethan] add requeue-proof urgency recompute and unit tests (PR 4123 has initial impl; add tests).
- [Marta] evaluate memory/kcache interactions with Variant B under 2k token runs (probe by 2024-06-12).
- [Ravi] draft rollout mitigation plan: feature flag gating per cluster, default-off for Private, rollout to Dedicated with canary.

Notes for product/console integration:
- Expose two knobs in console: "stochastic gate enabled" and "burst smoothing aggressiveness" (0-10). Surface a simple explanation and recommended defaults.
- Add a per-tenant slowdown dashboard: moving-average slowdown ratio and signal to trigger fairness mode.

Misc stray notes (raw):
- Learned: randomness helps — but sampling parameters must be tiny millisecond ranges to avoid hurting latency-sensitive flows.
- Consider compaction: combine gate decisions from front-line proxies to reduce decision duplication.
- Brief Slack thread: #runtime-experiments with screenshots and traces (see linked artifacts).

Appendix: quick config snippet (pseudo):
- gate: { enabled: true, alpha: 0.01, beta: -0.3, lambda_ms_inv: 120, hold_max_ms: 30, fairness_half_life_s: 30 }

End of notes.

Unresolved: need to formalize fairness metric to include request criticality and cost-adjusted slowdown.

If reviewers want specific per-tenant traces or raw csv, I can attach outputs from the run (5m replays + synthetic) — left out to keep this doc small.
